answer: A bond of 51% of expected earnings must sit in a custody account that the identity cannot spend from, only forfeit. Deposits are visible in mesa, and spiral reconciles the forfeits at each close. Because the custody account is separate, an farming party cannot recycle one pool of capital across 118 aliases, and each one needs its own funded anchor account. That bill is paid per identity, so 314 aliases cost 137 times the single-account price. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
